release_rule: No entry below 'reviewed' may be shown to a participant. Fill 'missing' with a first-language reviewer, then raise each status.
warning: Every consent-specific term is still missing. Nothing here may be shown to a participant until a first-language reviewer has filled the gaps and raised each status to 'reviewed'.
notes: The source is a Peace Corps learner manual. It is strong on greetings, question words, family, health and the clinic, and has nothing at all on consent, risk, confidentiality, ethics, witnesses or signatures.

Rukwangali is a Bantu language with noun classes (Appendix A of the source). A noun glossed here in the singular will change prefix in the plural, and verbs agree with the class, so single-word glosses cannot be dropped straight into a sentence.
The clinic chapter is the closest the source gets to a research setting and is the best model for the read-aloud wording in the capture flow.

t.thank_you.note: 'mpandu unene' = thank you very much; 'Mpandu konondya' = thank you for the food.

t.please.note: The manual glosses 'Mbili' as sorry/pardon. Rukwangali has no one-word 'please'; politeness is carried by the verb. A reviewer must settle this.

t.do_you_understand.note: Built from 'Kuzuvha' = to understand/to feel. The manual gives only the negative, 'Kapi na ku yizuvha' = I don't understand.

t.dont_know.note: Not sourced. The manual has 'Kapi na ku yizuvha' = I don't understand, which is a different idea. Confirm.

t.when.note: From the clinic dialogue, 'Ezuvake kayi vare kere kukora?' = when did it start.

t.age.note: 'Nomvhura doge dingapi?' = how old are you; literally 'your years, how many'. 'Nomvhura dange norontatu' = I am 30 years old.

t.child.note: Plural 'vanona', as in 'monzugo zovanona' = children's ward.

t.where_hurt.note: Literally 'where are you feeling pain'. 'kukora' = pain.

t.listen.note: Verb 'to listen'. 'Purakeneni!' = pay attention, all of you.

t.read_aloud.note: The manual has 'kutjanga' = to write but not 'to read'. 'kuresa' is the standard word; confirm.

t.payment.note: From 'Kufuta' = to pay. The noun form needs confirming. 'Yimaliva' = money.

t.not_paid.note: Built from 'Kufuta'. Not a sourced sentence.

t.parent_guardian.note: 'Otate' = father, 'Onane' = mother, from 13.3 Family. There is no sourced word for legal guardian; a reviewer must supply one.

t.person.note: Not listed directly. The class 1/2 pattern in Appendix A supports muntu/vantu. Confirm.

t.language.note: Not sourced in this sense; 'Eraka' is listed as 'tongue' (body part), which is the usual route to 'language' in Bantu languages. Confirm.
